excludes: Broad WCAG remediation is owned by accessibility-implement.
General frontend refactoring is owned by frontend-refactor.
General component/page implementation is owned by frontend-implement.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement modal and nonmodal dialog interactions with appropriate semantics, focus and dismissal behavior, layering, unsaved-state protection, and idempotent consequential actions.

provenance.claim_scope: modal dialog focus and inertness semantics

risk.rationale: modal-dialog-patterns changes repository code and browser/server behavior; mutations remain limited to the explicitly requested scope and require affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Repair focus order, landmarks, live regions, accessible names, color contrast, keyboard support and screen-reader issues across the complete application.
Refactor existing frontend components for stronger types, smaller responsibilities, reuse, framework idioms and maintainability without changing overlay behavior.

positive.prompt: Implement a modal editor launched from a virtualized row. It must choose safe initial focus, make the background inert, guard unsaved input, compose with a popover, and restore focus when the original row was deleted.

Implement an accessible destructive confirmation whose request can time out after server commit. Define dismissal during submission, stable operation identity, server authorization/idempotency, conflict handling and persisted-outcome verification.

assertions.criterion: Owns dialog/modal semantic choice, focus, dismissal, layering and dialog-contained mutation behavior while leaving broad accessibility and refactoring work to neighbors.
Inspects installed dialog/design-system primitive, browser targets, layer/scroll manager, trigger lifecycle, mutation contract, authorization and tests from the fixture without inventing APIs.
Chooses modal versus nonmodal semantics and consequence-aware focus/dismissal first, verifies primitive capability, then defines layer, unsaved-state and mutation failure behavior.

Does not label interactive-background surfaces modal, selects initial and return focus contextually, prevents unsafe pointer dismissal, handles missing invokers and uses server authorization plus stable idempotency for consequential actions.

Tests keyboard/screen reader, background inertness or nonmodal access, nested layers, invoker removal, pointer drag/selection, rapid lifecycle, zoom/mobile/reduced motion and duplicate/timeout/conflict mutation outcomes.
Reports interaction/dismissal semantics, focus/layer ownership, mutation/unsaved-state contract, installed capability, checks and residual browser/assistive-technology risk.
Composes with the repository primitive and layer tokens, avoids global duplicate listeners and keeps semantics independent of visual shape or fixed z-index/timing values.

scenarios.prompt: A custom overlay marks every drawer modal, always focuses the first control, closes on pointer-down anywhere outside, assumes its trigger still exists, and prevents duplicates only by disabling the confirm button. Repair the interaction.

assertions.criterion: Resolves exact actor, tenant, target, consequence, operation identity, authorization, pending/unknown outcome, cancellation and recovery behavior before allowing retry or dismissal.
Uses server-side idempotency and authorization, does not discard state during ambiguous completion, reconciles outcome and restores focus to a meaningful surviving workflow target.
Requires persisted server and caller-visible outcome under double activation and timeout-after-commit plus keyboard/focus evidence; a disabled button or closed dialog is not proof.

scenarios.prompt: A destructive account dialog currently closes on outside pointer-down while a request is pending; the user retries after a timeout and the trigger row disappears. Explain the safe mutation and focus behavior.

assertions.criterion: Derives stack evidence from the lockfile, installed types, target-browser behavior and matching official documentation; applies only exposed callbacks and treats package migration separately, without requiring a particular helper command.
Checks framework, primitive, portal/layer manager, browser targets and test environment as one compatibility unit.
Anchors semantics in WAI-ARIA and HTML behavior while isolating volatile framework callback names and avoiding remembered support claims.

scenarios.prompt: The application pins a supported dialog primitive whose current documentation uses newer focus and outside-interaction callbacks. Native dialog support also varies across target browsers. No upgrade is authorized.
